# PRACTICE DIRECTION 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS

# This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61] Contents of this Practice Direction

## 61.1 – Scope

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 61.1 – Scope] 1.1 Practice Direction 58 also applies to Admiralty claims except where it is inconsistent with Part 61 or this practice direction.

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 61.1 – Scope] 1.2 Practice Direction 57AC (Witness Evidence at Trial) applies to witness statements for use at trials in admiralty claims (including claims in rem, collision claims, and limitation claims) in the Admiralty Court, notwithstanding that such claims are not proceedings under CPR Part 7 or Part 8. It applies to proceedings in the Admiralty Court whenever begun, but only to trial witness statements signed on or after 1 October 2021.

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 61.1 – Scope] (Rule 61.1(2) defines an ‘admiralty claim’ as a claim within the Admiralty jurisdiction of the High Court as set out in section 20 of the Senior Courts Act 1981.)”

## Case management

## 2.1 After a claim form is issued the Registrar will issue a direction in writing stating –

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 2.1 After a claim form is issued the Registrar will issue a direction in writing stating –] (1) whether the claim will remain in the Admiralty Court or be transferred to another court; and

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 2.1 After a claim form is issued the Registrar will issue a direction in writing stating –] (2) if the claim remains in the Admiralty Court –

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 2.1 After a claim form is issued the Registrar will issue a direction in writing stating –] (a) whether it will be dealt with by –

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 2.1 After a claim form is issued the Registrar will issue a direction in writing stating –] (i) the Admiralty Judge; or

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 2.1 After a claim form is issued the Registrar will issue a direction in writing stating –] (ii) the Registrar; and

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 2.1 After a claim form is issued the Registrar will issue a direction in writing stating –] (b) whether the trial will be in London or elsewhere.

## 2.2 In making these directions the Registrar will have regard to –

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 2.2 In making these directions the Registrar will have regard to –] (1) the nature of the issues and the sums in dispute; and

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 2.2 In making these directions the Registrar will have regard to –] (2) the criteria set in rule 26.13 so far as they are applicable.

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 2.2 In making these directions the Registrar will have regard to –] 2.3 Where the Registrar directs that the claim will be dealt with by the Admiralty Judge, case management directions will be given and any case management conference or pre-trial review will be heard by the Admiralty Judge.

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 2.2 In making these directions the Registrar will have regard to –] 2.4 Where it is directed that a claim is to be dealt with by the Registrar, it is the Registrar who will give directions, conduct any case management conference and any pre-trial review, and try the claim.

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 2.2 In making these directions the Registrar will have regard to –] 2.5 Appeals from all decisions and judgments of the Registrar are to the Admiralty Judge, unless otherwise ordered (and subject to article 4(1)(a) of the Access to Justice 1999 (Destination of Appeals) Order 2016, S.I. 2016 No. 917).

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 2.2 In making these directions the Registrar will have regard to –] 2.6 A personal injury or fatal accident claim must be commenced in the Admiralty Court if it is made in rem or if it arises out of a collision; see CPR rules 61.2(1)(a)(i) and (ii).

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 2.2 In making these directions the Registrar will have regard to –] 2.7 Personal injury and fatal accident claims falling within section 20(2)(f) of the Senior Courts Act 1981 made in personam, if commenced in the High Court, may be commenced in the Admiralty Court.  Under its tort and contract jurisdiction and its jurisdiction to determine claims for sums recoverable under statute conferred by sections 15 and 16 of the County Courts Act 1984 respectively, such claims may also be commenced in the County Court.

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 2.2 In making these directions the Registrar will have regard to –] 2.8 Claims within paragraph 2.7 should not be commenced in the Admiralty Court unless they require or would benefit from the specialist knowledge and experience of that court.  That is likely to include personal injury claims—

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 2.2 In making these directions the Registrar will have regard to –] (a) which involve questions of navigation, seamanship, boat or ship-handling skills and/or acts or omissions relating to sea state;

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 2.2 In making these directions the Registrar will have regard to –] (b) which arise out of the shipwreck, capsizing or stranding of the ship, or explosion or fire in the ship;

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 2.2 In making these directions the Registrar will have regard to –] (c) which are employer’s liability claims relating to or concerning equipment or working practices peculiar to a ship;

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 2.2 In making these directions the Registrar will have regard to –] (d) which raise difficult or novel questions of private international law or of the interpretation of the Athens Convention.

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 2.2 In making these directions the Registrar will have regard to –] Other personal injury claims not raising any such issues should ordinarily be commenced in the County Court or the Central Office of the King’s Bench Division of the High Court.

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 2.2 In making these directions the Registrar will have regard to –] 2.9 Where a personal injury or fatal accident claim in personam has been commenced in the Admiralty Court but, at any stage, it appears that it may be more efficiently or proportionately tried in another court, then it may be transferred to that other court on the application of any party or of the court’s own motion (see CPR rule 61.2(3)).  The County Court has similar powers under CPR rule 30.3, including the power to transfer to the Admiralty Court.

## 61.3 – Claims in rem

## 3.1 A claim form in rem must be in Form ADM1.

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 3.1 A claim form in rem must be in Form ADM1.] 3.2 The claimant in a claim in rem may be named or may be described, but if not named in the claim form must identify himself by name if requested to do so by any other party.

## 3.3 The defendant must be described in the claim form.

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 3.3 The defendant must be described in the claim form.] 3.4 The acknowledgment of service must be in Form ADM2. The person who acknowledges service must identify himself by name.

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 3.3 The defendant must be described in the claim form.] 3.5 The period for acknowledging service under rule 61.3(4) applies irrespective of whether the claim form contains particulars of claim.

## 3.6 A claim form in rem may be served in the following ways:

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 3.6 A claim form in rem may be served in the following ways:] (1) on the property against which the claim is brought by fixing a copy of the claim form –

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 3.6 A claim form in rem may be served in the following ways:] (a) on the outside of the property in a position which may reasonably be expected to be seen; or

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 3.6 A claim form in rem may be served in the following ways:] (b) where the property is freight, either –

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 3.6 A claim form in rem may be served in the following ways:] (i) on the cargo in respect of which the freight was earned; or

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 3.6 A claim form in rem may be served in the following ways:] (ii) on the ship on which the cargo was carried;

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 3.6 A claim form in rem may be served in the following ways:] (2) if the property to be served is in the custody of a person who will not permit access to it, by leaving a copy of the claim form with that person;

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 3.6 A claim form in rem may be served in the following ways:] (3) where the property has been sold by the Marshal, by filing the claim form at the court;

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 3.6 A claim form in rem may be served in the following ways:] (4) where there is a notice against arrest, on the person named in the notice as being authorised to accept service;

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 3.6 A claim form in rem may be served in the following ways:] (5) on any solicitor authorised to accept service;

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 3.6 A claim form in rem may be served in the following ways:] (6) in accordance with any agreement providing for service of proceedings; or

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 3.6 A claim form in rem may be served in the following ways:] (7) in any other manner as the court may direct under rule 6.15 provided that the property against which the claim is brought or part of it is within the jurisdiction of the court.

## 3.7 In claims where the property –

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 3.7 In claims where the property –] (1) is to be arrested; or

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 3.7 In claims where the property –] (2) is already under arrest in current proceedings,

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 3.7 In claims where the property –] the Marshal will serve the in rem claim form if the claimant requests the court to do so.

## 3.8 In all other cases in rem claim forms must be served by the claimant.

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 3.8 In all other cases in rem claim forms must be served by the claimant.] 3.9 Where the defendants are described and not named on the claim form (for example as ‘the Owners of the Ship X’), any acknowledgment of service in addition to stating that description must also state the full names of the persons acknowledging service and the nature of their ownership.

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 3.8 In all other cases in rem claim forms must be served by the claimant.] 3.10 After the acknowledgment of service has been filed, the claim will follow the procedure applicable to a claim proceeding in the Commercial list except that the claimant is allowed 75 days to serve the particulars of claim.

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 3.8 In all other cases in rem claim forms must be served by the claimant.] 3.11 A defendant who files an acknowledgment of service to an in rem claim does not lose any right he may have to dispute the jurisdiction of the court (see rule 10.1(3)(b) and Part 11).

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 3.8 In all other cases in rem claim forms must be served by the claimant.] 3.12 Any person who pays the prescribed fee may, during office hours, search for, inspect and take a copy of any claim form in rem whether or not it has been served.

## 61.3A – Claims in personam

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 61.3A – Claims in personam] 3A.1 This section applies to Admiralty claims in personam (defined in rule 61.1(2)(bc) as an admiralty claim other than a claim in rem). Subject to the provisions of Part 61 and this practice direction relating to limitation claims and to collision claims, the following provisions apply to such claims.

## 3A.2 All such claims will proceed in accordance with Part 58 (Commercial Court).

## 3A.3 The claim form must be in Form ADM1A and must be served by the claimant.

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 3A.3 The claim form must be in Form ADM1A and must be served by the claimant.] 3A.4 The claimant may be named or may be described, but if not named in the claim form must identify themselves by name if requested to do so by any other party.

## 3A.5 The defendant must be named in the claim form.

## 3A.6 Any person who files a defence must identify themselves by name in the defence.

## 61.4 – Collision claims

## 4.1 A collision statement of case must be in form ADM3 .

## 4.2 A collision statement of case must contain –

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 4.2 A collision statement of case must contain –] (1) in Part 1 of the form, answers to the questions set out in that Part; and

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 4.2 A collision statement of case must contain –] (2)  in Part 2 of the form–

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 4.2 A collision statement of case must contain –] (a)full particulars of—

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 4.2 A collision statement of case must contain –] (i) the sequence of material events leading up to the collision;

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 4.2 A collision statement of case must contain –] (ii) all allegations of causative negligence or other fault which the party filing the collision statement of case makes, and

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 4.2 A collision statement of case must contain –] (iii)  any other material facts and matters on which that party relies; and

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 4.2 A collision statement of case must contain –] (b)a statement of the relief or remedy which the party filing the collision statement of case claims.

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 4.2 A collision statement of case must contain –] 4.3 When he files his collision statement of case each party must give notice to every other party that he has done so.

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 4.2 A collision statement of case must contain –] 4.4 Within 14 days after the last collision statement of case is filed each party must serve a copy of his collision statement of case on every other party.

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 4.2 A collision statement of case must contain –] 4.5 Before the coming into force of Part 61, a collision statement of case was known as a Preliminary Act and the law relating to Preliminary Acts will continue to apply to collision statements of case.

## 4.5A

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 4.5A] (1)In any collision defence, a party must state –

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 4.5A] (a)  which of the allegations in Part 2 of the collision statement of case the party denies;

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 4.5A] (b)which such allegations the party is unable to admit or deny, but requires the other party to prove; and

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 4.5A] (c) which such allegations the party admits.

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 4.5A] (2)Where a party denies an allegation in Part 2 of the other party’s collision statement of case–

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 4.5A] (a)  the collision defence must state the reasons for doing so; and

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 4.5A] (b)if a different version of events from that given by the other party is to be put forward, the collision defence must state that version (which, where appropriate, may be done by reference to the party’s own collision statement of case).

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 4.5A] (3)A party who—

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 4.5A] (a)fails to deal with an allegation in Part 2 of another party’s collision statement of case; but

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 4.5A] (b)has set out in a collision defence a case in relation to the issue to which that allegation is relevant, shall be taken to require that allegation to be proved.

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 4.5A] (4)Subject to paragraph (3), a party who fails to deal with an allegation in Part 2 of another party’s collision statement of case shall be taken to admit that allegation.

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 4.5A] 4.5B When a collision defence is filed, the party filing must give notice of that filing to every other party.

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 4.5A] 4.5C Within 14 days after the last collision defence is filed each party must serve a copy of their collision defence on every other party.

## 4.5D If a collision reply is filed, the party filing must–

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 4.5D If a collision reply is filed, the party filing must–] (a)give notice of that filing to every other party; and

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 4.5D If a collision reply is filed, the party filing must–] (b)serve a copy of the collision reply on every other party (i) within 14 days after the last collision reply is filed, or (ii) where no other collision reply is filed, within 35 days after the last collision defence was filed.

## Case Management

## 4.6 In all collision claims—

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 4.6 In all collision claims—] (1) a case management conference is mandatory;

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 4.6 In all collision claims—] (2) the claimant must apply for a case management conference within 7 days after the last collision defence is filed, failing which any other party may apply for a case management conference;

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 4.6 In all collision claims—] (3) the mandatory case management conference will normally take place on the first available date 6 weeks after the last collision defence is filed.

## Fast track collision claims

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > Fast track collision claims] 4.7 In any collision claim where electronic track data has been disclosed by one or more parties as being in its control in accordance with rule 61.4(4A)—

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > Fast track collision claims] (1) the court will seek to adopt fast track procedures for the determination of issues of liability as part of its duty actively to manage cases in accordance with the overriding objective, which may include directions—

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > Fast track collision claims] (a) limiting further disclosure to contemporaneous documents made shortly before and shortly after the collision;

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > Fast track collision claims] (b) limiting witnesses to those most closely involved with the collision;

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > Fast track collision claims] (c) excluding or limiting expert evidence;

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > Fast track collision claims] (d) requiring the parties to provide a memorandum of points of agreement and dispute, to include an agreed plot of each vessel’s track leading up to the collision;

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > Fast track collision claims] (e) dispensing with oral evidence;

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > Fast track collision claims] (f) limiting the number of assessors to one, or dispensing with the assistance of assessors;

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > Fast track collision claims] (g) dispensing with an oral hearing, and instead determining issues of liability only on the basis of—

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > Fast track collision claims] (i) an agreed bundle of evidence, and

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > Fast track collision claims] (ii) written submissions, limited to 10 pages or such other length as is approved by the court, on fault, causation and apportionment, in which case the court will identify the date on which the trial will be deemed to start for the purposes of rule 61.4(10)(a);

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > Fast track collision claims] (h) allocating the case to a deputy High Court Judge sitting in the Admiralty Court, or to the Admiralty Registrar; and/or

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > Fast track collision claims] (i) making a costs capping order.

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > Fast track collision claims] (2) The parties should give careful consideration to adopting these and/or other procedures and directions when completing their case management information sheets. The court will give due consideration to any agreement made by the parties which is intended to dispose of the claim in an expeditious and cost-effective manner.

## Shorter and flexible trials of collision cases

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > Shorter and flexible trials of collision cases] 4.8 In a collision action to which rule 61.4(4A) and paragraph 4.7 of this practice direction do not apply, the parties will be expected to consider whether the claim is suitable to tried in accordance with Practice Direction 57AB (Shorter and Flexible Trial Schemes).

## 4.9 Practice Direction 57AB applies to collision claims with the following modifications—

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 4.9 Practice Direction 57AB applies to collision claims with the following modifications—] (1) paragraphs 2.09 to 2.34 do not apply and paragraphs 4.1 to 4.6 of this practice direction will apply instead; and

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 4.9 Practice Direction 57AB applies to collision claims with the following modifications—] (2) at the case management conference, in exercising its powers under PD57AB, the court will consider the options in paragraph 4.7(1)(a) to (i) above.

## 61.5 – Arrest

## 5.1 An application for arrest must be –

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 5.1 An application for arrest must be –] (1) in form ADM4 (which must also contain an undertaking); and

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 5.1 An application for arrest must be –] (2) accompanied by a declaration in form ADM5 .

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 5.1 An application for arrest must be –] 5.2 When it receives an application for arrest that complies with the rules and the practice direction the court will issue an arrest warrant.

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 5.1 An application for arrest must be –] 5.3 The declaration required by rule 61.5(3)(b) must be verified by a statement of truth and must state –

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 5.1 An application for arrest must be –] (1) in every claim –

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 5.1 An application for arrest must be –] (a) the nature of the claim or counterclaim and that it has not been satisfied and if it arises in connection with a ship, the name of that ship;

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 5.1 An application for arrest must be –] (b) the nature of the property to be arrested and, if the property is a ship, the name of the ship and her port of registry; and

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 5.1 An application for arrest must be –] (c) the amount of the security sought, if any.

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 5.1 An application for arrest must be –] (2) in a claim against a ship by virtue of section 21(4) of the Senior Courts Act 1981 –

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 5.1 An application for arrest must be –] (a) the name of the person who would be liable on the claim if it were not commenced in rem;

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 5.1 An application for arrest must be –] (b) that the person referred to in sub-paragraph (a) was, when the right to bring the claim arose –

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 5.1 An application for arrest must be –] (i) the owner or charterer of; or

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 5.1 An application for arrest must be –] (ii) in possession or in control of,

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 5.1 An application for arrest must be –] the ship in connection with which the claim arose; and

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 5.1 An application for arrest must be –] (c) that at the time the claim form was issued the person referred to in sub-paragraph (a) was either –

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 5.1 An application for arrest must be –] (i) the beneficial owner of all the shares in the ship in respect of which the warrant is required; or

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 5.1 An application for arrest must be –] (ii) the charterer of it under a charter by demise;

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 5.1 An application for arrest must be –] (3) in the cases set out in rules 61.5 (5) and (6) that the relevant notice has been sent or served, as appropriate; and

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 5.1 An application for arrest must be –] (4) in the case of a claim in respect of liability incurred under section 153 of the Merchant Shipping Act 1995, the facts relied on as establishing that the court is not prevented from considering the claim by reason of section 166(2) of that Act.

## 5.4 The notice required by rule 61.5(5)(a) must be in form ADM6 .

## 5.5 Property is arrested –

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 5.5 Property is arrested –] (1) by service on it of an arrest warrant in form ADM9 in the manner set out at paragraph 3.6(1); or

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 5.5 Property is arrested –] (2) where it is not reasonably practicable to serve the warrant, by service of a notice of the issue of the warrant –

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 5.5 Property is arrested –] (a) in the manner set out in paragraph 3.6(1) on the property; or

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 5.5 Property is arrested –] (b) by giving notice to those in charge of the property.

## 5.6 When property is arrested the Registrar will issue standard directions in form ADM10.

## 5.7 The Marshal does not insure property under arrest.

## 61.7 – Cautions against arrest

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 61.7 – Cautions against arrest] 6.1 The entry of a caution against arrest is not treated as a submission to the jurisdiction of the court.

## 6.2 The request for a caution against arrest must be in form ADM7 .

## 6.3 On the filing of such a request, a caution against arrest will be entered in the Register.

## 6.4 The Register is open for inspection when the Admiralty and Commercial Registry is open.

## 61.8 – Release and cautions against release

## 7.1 The request for a caution against release must be in form ADM11.

## 7.2 On the filing of such a request, a caution against release will be entered in the Register.

## 7.3 The Register is open for inspection when the Admiralty and Commercial Registry is open.

## 7.4 A request for release under rule 61.8(4)(c) and (d) must be in form ADM12.

## 7.5 A withdrawal of a caution against release must be in form ADM12A.

## 61.9 – Judgment in default

## 8.1 An application notice for judgment in default must be in form ADM13.

## 61.10 – Sale by the court and priorities

## 9.1 Any application to the court concerning –

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 9.1 Any application to the court concerning –] (1) the sale of the property under arrest; or

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 9.1 Any application to the court concerning –] (2) the proceeds of sale of property sold by the court

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 9.1 Any application to the court concerning –] will be heard in public and the application notice served on –

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 9.1 Any application to the court concerning –] (a) all parties to the claim;

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 9.1 Any application to the court concerning –] (b) all persons who have requested cautions against release with regard to the property or the proceeds of sale; and

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 9.1 Any application to the court concerning –] (c) the Marshal.

## 9.2 Unless the court orders otherwise an order for sale will be in form ADM14.

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 9.2 Unless the court orders otherwise an order for sale will be in form ADM14.] 9.3 Unless the Admiralty Judge orders otherwise, an order for sale before judgment may only be made by the Admiralty Judge.

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 9.2 Unless the court orders otherwise an order for sale will be in form ADM14.] 9.4 Unless the Admiralty Judge orders otherwise, a determination of priorities may only be made by the Admiralty Judge.

## 9.5 When –

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 9.5 When –] (1) proceeds of sale are paid into court by the Marshal; and

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 9.5 When –] (2) such proceeds are in a foreign currency,

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 9.5 When –] the funds will be placed on one day call interest bearing account unless the court orders otherwise.

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 9.5 When –] 9.6 Unless made at the same time as an application for sale, or other prior application, an application to place foreign currency on longer term deposit may be made to the Registrar.

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 9.5 When –] 9.7 Notice of the placement of foreign currency in an interest bearing account must be given to all parties interested in the fund by the party who made the application under paragraph 9.6.

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 9.5 When –] 9.8 Any interested party who wishes to object to the mode of investment of foreign currency paid into court may apply to the Registrar for directions.

## 61.11 – Limitation claims

## 10.1 The claim form in a limitation claim must be –

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 10.1 The claim form in a limitation claim must be –] (1) in form ADM15; and

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 10.1 The claim form in a limitation claim must be –] (2) accompanied by a declaration –

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 10.1 The claim form in a limitation claim must be –] (a) setting out the facts upon which the claimant relies; and

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 10.1 The claim form in a limitation claim must be –] (b) stating the names and addresses (if known) of all persons who, to the knowledge of the claimant, have claims against him in respect of the occurrence to which the limitation claim relates (other than named defendants and interested parties), verified by a statement of truth.

## 10.2 A defence to a limitation claim must be in form ADM16A.

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 10.2 A defence to a limitation claim must be in form ADM16A.] 10.3 A notice admitting the right of the claimant to limit liability in a limitation claim must be in form ADM16.

Document: Practice Direction 61
Section: 10.4 An acknowledgment of service in a limitation claim must be in form ADM16B.
Part 2 of 2
==================================================
## 10.4 An acknowledgment of service in a limitation claim must be in form ADM16B.

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 10.4 An acknowledgment of service in a limitation claim must be in form ADM16B.] 10.5 An application for a restricted limitation decree must be in form ADM17 and the decree issued by the court on such an application must be in form ADM18.

## 10.6 An application for a general limitation decree must be in form ADM17A.

## 10.7 Where –

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 10.7 Where –] (1) the right to limit is not admitted; and

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 10.7 Where –] (2) the claimant seeks a general limitation decree in form ADM17A,

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 10.7 Where –] the claimant must, within 7 days after the date of the filing of the defence of the defendant last served or the expiry of the time for doing so, apply for an appointment before the Registrar for a case management conference.

## 10.8 On an application under rule 61.11(12) the Registrar may –

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 10.8 On an application under rule 61.11(12) the Registrar may –] (1) grant a general limitation decree; or

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 10.8 On an application under rule 61.11(12) the Registrar may –] (2) if he does not grant a decree –

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 10.8 On an application under rule 61.11(12) the Registrar may –] (a) order service of a defence; and

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 10.8 On an application under rule 61.11(12) the Registrar may –] (c) make such other case management directions as may be appropriate.

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 10.8 On an application under rule 61.11(12) the Registrar may –] 10.9 The fact that a limitation fund has lapsed under rule 61.11(20)(a) does not prevent the establishment of a new fund.

## 10.9A A limitation fund may be constituted by—

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 10.9A A limitation fund may be constituted by—] (1) making a payment into court;

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 10.9A A limitation fund may be constituted by—] (2) providing court-approved security; or

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 10.9A A limitation fund may be constituted by—] (3) a combination of (1) and (2).

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 10.9A A limitation fund may be constituted by—] 10.10 Where a limitation fund is established by making a payment into court, the sum paid in must be –

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 10.9A A limitation fund may be constituted by—] (1) the sterling equivalent of the number of special drawing rights to which [the claimant] claims to be entitled to limit his liability under the Merchant Shipping Act 1995; together with

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 10.9A A limitation fund may be constituted by—] (2) interest from the date of the occurrence giving rise to his liability to the date of payment into court.

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 10.9A A limitation fund may be constituted by—] 10.11 Where the claimant does not know the sterling equivalent referred to in paragraph 10.10(1) on the date of payment into court he may –

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 10.9A A limitation fund may be constituted by—] (1) calculate it on the basis of the latest available published sterling equivalent of a special drawing right as fixed by the International Monetary Fund; and

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 10.9A A limitation fund may be constituted by—] (2) in the event of the sterling equivalent of a special drawing right on the date of payment into court being different from that used for calculating the amount of that payment into court the claimant may –

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 10.9A A limitation fund may be constituted by—] (a) make up any deficiency by making a further payment into court which, if made within 14 days after the payment into court, will be treated, except for the purpose of the rules relating to the accrual of interest on money paid into court, as if made on the date of that payment into court; or

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 10.9A A limitation fund may be constituted by—] (b) apply to the court for payment out of any excess amount (together with any interest accrued) paid into court.

## 10.12 An application under paragraph 10.11(2)(b) –

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 10.12 An application under paragraph 10.11(2)(b) –] (1) may be made without notice; and

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 10.12 An application under paragraph 10.11(2)(b) –] (2) must be supported by evidence proving, to the satisfaction of the court, the sterling equivalent of the appropriate number of special drawing rights on the date of payment into court.

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 10.12 An application under paragraph 10.11(2)(b) –] 10.13 The claimant must give notice in writing to every defendant and interested party whose address the claimant knows, of –

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 10.12 An application under paragraph 10.11(2)(b) –] (1) any payment into court specifying –

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 10.12 An application under paragraph 10.11(2)(b) –] (a) the date of the payment in;

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 10.12 An application under paragraph 10.11(2)(b) –] (b) the amount paid in and how it has been calculated;

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 10.12 An application under paragraph 10.11(2)(b) –] (c) the amount and rate of interest included; and

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 10.12 An application under paragraph 10.11(2)(b) –] (d) the period to which it relates; and

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 10.12 An application under paragraph 10.11(2)(b) –] (2) any excess amount (and interest) paid out to him under paragraph 10.11(2)(b).

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 10.12 An application under paragraph 10.11(2)(b) –] 10.13A Where a claimant wishes to establish a limitation fund (in whole or in part) by providing security, the claimant must apply to the court for an order approving the security.  The application may be made on paper and without notice, but the applicant should first seek to agree the provider, form, nature, and terms of the proposed security with any named defendant and any interested party before making the application (unless the circumstances of the case make that impracticable).

## 10.13B An application under paragraph 10.13A must be –

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 10.13B An application under paragraph 10.13A must be –] (1) accompanied by the proposed security or a draft thereof; and

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 10.13B An application under paragraph 10.13A must be –] (2) supported by evidence of—

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 10.13B An application under paragraph 10.13A must be –] (a) the adequacy of the proposed security; and

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 10.13B An application under paragraph 10.13A must be –] (b) if the proposed security is expressed in sterling, the sterling equivalent of the appropriate number of special drawing rights on the date the application is made.

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 10.13B An application under paragraph 10.13A must be –] 10.13C The court shall approve the proposed security if it is satisfied that it is adequate in all the circumstances (including its form, nature, terms, and the financial standing of the person offering it).

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 10.13B An application under paragraph 10.13A must be –] 10.13D Where a limitation fund is established (in whole or in part) by providing court-approved security, the security may be expressed in special drawing rights or sterling. If the security is expressed in sterling, the amount of the security shall be the same as if the fund were being constituted by payment in to court and paragraphs 10.10 and 10.11(1) above shall apply in an equivalent sense.

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 10.13B An application under paragraph 10.13A must be –] 10.13E The claimant must give notice in writing to every named defendant and any interested party whose address is known of any court-approved security lodged at court, specifying—

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 10.13B An application under paragraph 10.13A must be –] (1) the terms of the security;

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 10.13B An application under paragraph 10.13A must be –] (2) the date on which the security was lodged at court;

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 10.13B An application under paragraph 10.13A must be –] (3) how the amount of security was calculated;

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 10.13B An application under paragraph 10.13A must be –] (4) the amount and rate of interest included, and the period to which it relates,

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 10.13B An application under paragraph 10.13A must be –] and shall provide on request any person so notified with a copy of the security so lodged and the application made under paragraph 10.13A.

## 10.13F An application to set aside the court’s approval of a security may be made by—

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 10.13F An application to set aside the court’s approval of a security may be made by—] (1) any person (whether a defendant, an interested party or another), who was not given notice of the claimant’s application under paragraph 10.13A; or

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 10.13F An application to set aside the court’s approval of a security may be made by—] (2) any person (whether a defendant, an interested party or another) if circumstances relevant to the adequacy of the security have changed since it was approved by the court.

## 10.13G An application under paragraph 10.13F(1) must be –

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 10.13G An application under paragraph 10.13F(1) must be –] (1) made on notice to the provider of the security, all claimants, all named defendants, and all interested parties (whose addresses are known);

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 10.13G An application under paragraph 10.13F(1) must be –] (2) supported by evidence setting out the reasons why the court’s approval of the security should be set aside; and

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 10.13G An application under paragraph 10.13F(1) must be –] (3) made within 21 days of receipt by the applicant of notice given under paragraph 10.13E (if such notice was given to the applicant) or as soon as reasonably practicable (if no such notice was given to the applicant).

## 10.13H An application under paragraph 10.13F(2) must be—

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 10.13H An application under paragraph 10.13F(2) must be—] (1) made on notice to the provider of the security, all claimants, all named defendants, and all Interested Parties (whose addresses are known);

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 10.13H An application under paragraph 10.13F(2) must be—] (2) supported by evidence setting out the change in circumstances justifying the setting aside of the court’s approval of the security; and

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 10.13H An application under paragraph 10.13F(2) must be—] (3) made as soon as reasonably practicable after discovery of the change of circumstances.

## 10.13I On an application under paragraph 10.13F, the court may—

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 10.13I On an application under paragraph 10.13F, the court may—] (1) confirm its approval of the adequacy of the security;

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 10.13I On an application under paragraph 10.13F, the court may—] (2) set aside its approval of the adequacy of the security; and/or

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 10.13I On an application under paragraph 10.13F, the court may—] (3) require the fund to be reconstituted in such manner and on such terms as it thinks fit.

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 10.13I On an application under paragraph 10.13F, the court may—] 10.13J If a claimant has constituted a fund by payment in of money, it may apply at any time for an order permitting the reconstitution of the fund (in whole or in part) by means of a court-approved security. Any such application shall be made in accordance with paragraphs 10.13A to 10.13E, and paragraphs 10.13F to 10.13I shall apply to any order made.”.

## 10.14 A claim against the fund must be in form ADM20 .

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 10.14 A claim against the fund must be in form ADM20 .] 10.15 A defendant’s statement of case filed and served in accordance with rule 61.11(15) must contain particulars of the defendant’s claim.

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 10.14 A claim against the fund must be in form ADM20 .] 10.16 Any defendant who is unable to file and serve a statement of case in accordance with rule 61.11(15) and paragraph 10.15 must file a declaration, verified by a statement of truth, in form ADM21 stating the reason for his inability.

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 10.14 A claim against the fund must be in form ADM20 .] 10.17 No later than 7 days after the time for filing claims [or declarations], the Registrar will fix a date for a case management conference at which directions will be given for the further conduct of the proceedings.

## 10.18 Nothing in rule 61.11 prevents limitation being relied on by way of defence.

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 10.18 Nothing in rule 61.11 prevents limitation being relied on by way of defence.] 11.1 For the purposes of section 177 of the Merchant Shipping Act 1995 (‘the Act’), the Fund may be given notice of proceedings by any party to a claim against an owner or guarantor in respect of liability under section 153 of the Act by that person serving a notice in writing on the Fund together with copies of the claim form and any statements of case served in the claim.

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 10.18 Nothing in rule 61.11 prevents limitation being relied on by way of defence.] 11.2 Notice given to the Fund under paragraph 11.1 shall be deemed to have been given to the Supplementary Fund.

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 10.18 Nothing in rule 61.11 prevents limitation being relied on by way of defence.] 11.3 The Fund or the Supplementary Fund may intervene in any claim to which paragraph 11.1 applies, (whether or not served with the notice), by serving notice of intervention on the –

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 10.18 Nothing in rule 61.11 prevents limitation being relied on by way of defence.] (1) owner;

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 10.18 Nothing in rule 61.11 prevents limitation being relied on by way of defence.] (2) guarantor; and

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 10.18 Nothing in rule 61.11 prevents limitation being relied on by way of defence.] (3) court.

## 11.4 Where a judgment is given against –

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 11.4 Where a judgment is given against –] (1) the Fund in any claim under section 175 of the Act;

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 11.4 Where a judgment is given against –] (2) the Supplementary Fund in any claim under section 176A of the Act, the Registrar will arrange for a stamped copy of the judgment to be sent by post to –

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 11.4 Where a judgment is given against –] (a) the Fund (where paragraph (1) applies);

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 11.4 Where a judgment is given against –] (b) the Supplementary Fund (where paragraph (2) applies).

## 11.5 Notice to the Registrar of the matters set out in –

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 11.5 Notice to the Registrar of the matters set out in –] (1) section 176(3)(b) of the Act in proceedings under section 175; or

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 11.5 Notice to the Registrar of the matters set out in –] (2) section 176B(2)(b) of the Act in proceedings under section 176A, must be given in writing and sent to the court by –

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 11.5 Notice to the Registrar of the matters set out in –] (a) the Fund (where paragraph (1) applies);

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 11.5 Notice to the Registrar of the matters set out in –] (b) the Supplementary Fund (where paragraph (2) applies).

## References to the Registrar

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > References to the Registrar] 13.1 The court may at any stage in the claim refer any question or issue for determination by the Registrar (a ‘reference’).

## 13.2 Unless the court orders otherwise, where a reference has been ordered –

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 13.2 Unless the court orders otherwise, where a reference has been ordered –] (1) if particulars of claim have not already been served, the claimant must file and serve particulars of claim on all other parties within 14 days after the date of the order;

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 13.2 Unless the court orders otherwise, where a reference has been ordered –] (2) any party opposing the claim must file a defence to the claim within 14 days after service of the particulars of claim on him;

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 13.2 Unless the court orders otherwise, where a reference has been ordered –] (3) the rules concerning statements of case shall apply to the particulars of claim, the defence and any other statements of case served in the reference; and

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 13.2 Unless the court orders otherwise, where a reference has been ordered –] (4) all documents which the claimant (or counterclaimant) in a reference intends to rely on in order to show that the sums claimed were properly incurred and paid (‘vouchers’) shall be appended to their first statement of case in the reference and cross referenced to the sums being claimed, unless there is a compelling reason not to do so.

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 13.2 Unless the court orders otherwise, where a reference has been ordered –] 13.3 Within 7 days after the defence is filed, the claimant must apply for an appointment before the Registrar for a case management conference.

## Undertakings

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > Undertakings] 14.1 Where, in or this practice direction, any undertaking to the Marshal is required it must be given –

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > Undertakings] (1) in writing and to his satisfaction; or

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > Undertakings] (2) in accordance with such other arrangements as he may require.

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > Undertakings] 14.2 Where any party is dissatisfied with a direction given by the Marshal in this respect he may apply to the Registrar for a ruling.

## Admiralty Claims

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > Admiralty Claims] Available on the forms page.

id: Practice Direction 62 – Arbitration
content:
# PRACTICE DIRECTION 62 – ARBITRATION

# This Practice Direction supplements Part 62

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 62] Contents of this Practice Direction

## SECTION I

## 1.1

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 62 > 1.1] This Section of this Practice Direction applies to arbitration claims to which Section I of Part 62 applies.

## 1.2

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 62 > 1.2] In this Section ‘the 1996 Act’ means the Arbitration Act 1996.

## 1.3

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 62 > 1.3] Where a rule provides for a document to be sent, it may be sent –

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 62 > 1.3] (1) by first class post;

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 62 > 1.3] (2) through a document exchange; or

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 62 > 1.3] (3) by fax, electronic mail or other means of electronic communication.

## 62.3 – Starting the claim

## 2.1

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 62 > 2.1] An arbitration claim under the 1996 Act (other than under section 9) must be started in accordance with the High Court and County Courts (Allocation of Arbitration Proceedings) Order 1996 by the issue of an arbitration claim form.

## 2.2

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 62 > 2.2] An arbitration claim form must be substantially in the form set out in Appendix A to this practice direction.

## 2.3

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 62 > 2.3] Subject to paragraph 2.1, an arbitration claim form –

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 62 > 2.3] (1) may be issued at the courts set out in column 1 of the table below and will be entered in the list set out against that court in column 2;

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 62 > 2.3] (2) relating to a landlord and tenant or partnership dispute must be issued in the Chancery Division of the High Court.

## 2.3A

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 62 > 2.3A] An arbitration claim form must, in the case of an appeal, or application for permission to appeal, from a judge-arbitrator, be issued in the Civil Division of the Court of Appeal. The judge hearing the application may adjourn the matter for oral argument before two judges of that court.

## 62.4 – Arbitration claim form

## Service

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 62 > Service] The court may exercise its powers under rule 6.15 to permit service of an arbitration claim form at the address of a party’s solicitor or representative acting for that party in the arbitration.

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 62 > Service] Where the arbitration claim form is served by the claimant he must file a certificate of service within 7 days of service of the arbitration claim form.

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 62 > Service] (Rule 6.17 specifies what a certificate of service must show).

## Acknowledgment of service or making representations by arbitrator or ACAS

## 4.1

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 62 > 4.1] Where –

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 62 > 4.1] (1) an arbitrator; or

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 62 > 4.1] (2) ACAS (in a claim under the 1996 Act as applied with modifications by the ACAS Arbitration Scheme (England and Wales) Order 2001)

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 62 > 4.1] is sent a copy of an arbitration claim form (including an arbitration claim form sent under rule 62.6(2)), that arbitrator or ACAS (as the case may be) may –

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 62 > 4.1] (a) apply to be made a defendant; or

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 62 > 4.1] (b) make representations to the court under paragraph 4.3.

## 4.2

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 62 > 4.2] An application under paragraph 4.1(2)(a) to be made a defendant –

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 62 > 4.2] (1) must be served on the claimant; but

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 62 > 4.2] (2) need not be served on any other party.

## 4.3

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 62 > 4.3] An arbitrator or ACAS may make representations by filing written evidence or in writing to the court.

## Supply of documents from court records

## 5.1

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 62 > 5.1] An arbitration claim form may only be inspected with the permission of the court.

## 62.7 – Case management

## 6.1

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 62 > 6.1] The following directions apply unless the court orders otherwise.

## 6.2

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 62 > 6.2] A defendant who wishes to rely on evidence before the court must file and serve his written evidence –

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 62 > 6.2] (1) within 21 days after the date by which he was required to acknowledge service; or,

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 62 > 6.2] (2) where a defendant is not required to file an acknowledgement of service, within 21 days after service of the arbitration claim form.

## 6.3

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 62 > 6.3] A claimant who wishes to rely on evidence in reply to written evidence filed under paragraph 6.2 must file and serve his written evidence within 7 days after service of the defendant’s evidence.

## 6.4

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 62 > 6.4] Agreed indexed and paginated bundles of all the evidence and other documents to be used at the hearing must be prepared by the claimant.

## 6.5

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 62 > 6.5] Not later than 5 days before the hearing date estimates for the length of the hearing must be filed together with a complete set of the documents to be used.

## 6.6

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 62 > 6.6] Not later than 2 days before the hearing date the claimant must file and serve –

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 62 > 6.6] (1) a chronology of the relevant events cross-referenced to the bundle of documents;

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 62 > 6.6] (2) (where necessary) a list of the persons involved; and

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 62 > 6.6] (3) a skeleton argument which lists succinctly –

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 62 > 6.6] (a) the issues which arise for decision;

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 62 > 6.6] (b) the grounds of relief (or opposing relief) to be relied upon;

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 62 > 6.6] (c) the submissions of fact to be made with the references to the evidence; and

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 62 > 6.6] (d) the submissions of law with references to the relevant authorities.

## 6.7

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 62 > 6.7] Not later than the day before the hearing date the defendant must file and serve a skeleton argument which lists succinctly –

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 62 > 6.7] (1) the issues which arise for decision;

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 62 > 6.7] (2) the grounds of relief (or opposing relief) to be relied upon;

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 62 > 6.7] (3) the submissions of fact to be made with the references to the evidence; and

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 62 > 6.7] (4) the submissions of law with references to the relevant authorities.

## Securing the attendance of witnesses

## 7.1

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 62 > 7.1] A party to arbitral proceedings being conducted in England or Wales who wishes to rely on section 43 of the 1996 Act to secure the attendance of a witness must apply for a witness summons in accordance with Part 34.

## 7.2

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 62 > 7.2] If the attendance of the witness is required within the district of a district registry, the application may be made at that registry.

## 7.3

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 62 > 7.3] A witness summons will not be issued until the applicant files written evidence showing that the application is made with –

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 62 > 7.3] (1) the permission of the tribunal; or

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 62 > 7.3] (2) the agreement of the other parties.

## Interim remedies

## 8.1

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 62 > 8.1] An application for an interim remedy under section 44 of the 1996 Act must be made in an arbitration claim form.

## 9.1 Omitted

## Decisions without a hearing

## 10.1

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 62 > 10.1] Having regard to the overriding objective the court may decide particular issues without a hearing.

## 10.2

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 62 > 10.2] The court will generally decide whether to extend the time limit under section 70(3) of the 1996 Act without a hearing. Where the court makes an order extending the time limit, the defendant must file his written evidence within 21 days from service of the order.

## 62.9 – Variation of time

## 11.1

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 62 > 11.1] An application for an order under rule 62.9(1) –

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 62 > 11.1] (1) before the period of 28 days has expired, must be made in a Part 23 application notice; and

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 62 > 11.1] (2) after the period of 28 days has expired, must be set out in a separately identified part in the arbitration claim form.

## Applications for permission to appeal

## 12.1

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 62 > 12.1] Where a party seeks permission to appeal to the court on a question of law arising out of an arbitration award, the arbitration claim form must, in addition to complying with rule 62.4(1) –

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 62 > 12.1] (1) identify the question of law;

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 62 > 12.1] (2) state the grounds (but not the argument) on which the party challenges the award and contends that permission should be given;

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 62 > 12.1] (3) be accompanied by a skeleton argument in support of the application in accordance with paragraph 12.2; and

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 62 > 12.1] (4) append the award.

## 12.2

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 62 > 12.2] Subject to paragraph 12.3, the skeleton argument –

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 62 > 12.2] (1) must be printed in 12 point font, with 1� line spacing;

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 62 > 12.2] (2) should not exceed 15 pages in length; and

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 62 > 12.2] (3) must contain an estimate of how long the court is likely to need to deal with the application on the papers.

## 12.3

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 62 > 12.3] If the skeleton argument exceeds 15 pages in length the author must write to the court explaining why that is necessary.

## 12.4

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 62 > 12.4] Written evidence may be filed in support of the application only if it is necessary to show (insofar as that is not apparent from the award itself) –

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 62 > 12.4] (1) that the determination of the question raised by the appeal will substantially affect the rights of one or more of the parties;

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 62 > 12.4] (2) that the question is one which the tribunal was asked to determine;

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 62 > 12.4] (3) that the question is one of general public importance;

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 62 > 12.4] (4) that it is just and proper in all the circumstances for the court to determine the question raised by the appeal.

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 62 > 12.4] Any such evidence must be filed and served with the arbitration claim form.

## 12.5

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 62 > 12.5] Unless there is a dispute whether the question raised by the appeal is one which the tribunal was asked to determine, no arbitration documents may be put before the court other than –

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 62 > 12.5] (1) the award; and

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 62 > 12.5] (2) any document (such as the contract or the relevant parts thereof) which is referred to in the award and which the court needs to read to determine a question of law arising out of the award.

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 62 > 12.5] In this Practice Direction ‘arbitration documents’ means documents adduced in or produced for the purposes of the arbitration.

## 12.6

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 62 > 12.6] A respondent who wishes to oppose an application for permission to appeal must file a respondent’s notice which –

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 62 > 12.6] (1) sets out the grounds (but not the argument) on which the respondent opposes the application; and

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 62 > 12.6] (2) states whether the respondent wishes to contend that the award should be upheld for reasons not expressed (or not fully expressed) in the award and, if so, states those reasons (but not the argument).

## 12.7

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 62 > 12.7] The respondent’s notice must be filed and served within 21 days after the date on which the respondent was required to acknowledge service and must be accompanied by a skeleton argument in support which complies with paragraph 12.2 above.

## 12.8

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 62 > 12.8] Written evidence in opposition to the application should be filed only if it complies with the requirements of paragraph 12.4 above. Any such evidence must be filed and served with the respondent’s notice.

## 12.9

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 62 > 12.9] The applicant may file and serve evidence or argument in reply only if it is necessary to do so. Any such evidence or argument must be as brief as possible and must be filed and served within 7 days after service of the respondent’s notice.

## 12.10

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 62 > 12.10] If either party wishes to invite the court to consider arbitration documents other than those specified in paragraph 12.5 above the counsel or solicitor responsible for settling the application documents must write to the court explaining why that is necessary.

## 12.11

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 62 > 12.11] If a party or its representative fails to comply with the requirements of paragraphs 12.1 to 12.9 the court may penalise that party or representative in costs.

## 12.12

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 62 > 12.12] The court will normally determine applications for permission to appeal without an oral hearing but may direct otherwise, particularly with a view to saving time (including court time) or costs.

## 12.13

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 62 > 12.13] Where the court considers that an oral hearing is required, it may give such further directions as are necessary.

## 12.14

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 62 > 12.14] Where the court refuses an application for permission to appeal without an oral hearing, it will provide brief reasons.

## 12.15

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 62 > 12.15] The bundle for the hearing of any appeal should contain only the claim form, the respondent’s notice, the arbitration documents referred to in paragraph 12.5, the order granting permission to appeal and the skeleton arguments.

## SECTION II

## 13.1

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 62 > 13.1] This Section of this Practice Direction applies to arbitration claims to which Section II of Part 62 applies.

## 62.13 – Starting the claim

## 14.1

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 62 > 14.1] An arbitration claim must be started in the Commercial Court and, where required to be heard by a judge, be heard by a judge of that court unless he otherwise directs.

## SECTION III

## 15.1

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 62 > 15.1] This Section of this Practice Direction applies to enforcement proceedings to which Section III of Part 62 applies.

## 62.21 – Registration of awards under the Arbitration (International Investment Disputes) Act 1966

## 16.1

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 62 > 16.1] Awards ordered to be registered under the 1966 Act and particulars will be entered in the Register kept for that purpose at the Admiralty and Commercial Registry.

## Arbitration

## N8 Claim form (arbitration)

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 62 > N8 Claim form (arbitration)] Available on the forms page.
