# Pre-Action Protocol for Judicial Review

# Pre-Action Protocol for Judicial Review

[Pre-Action Protocol for Judicial Review] Contents

## Introduction

[Pre-Action Protocol for Judicial Review > Introduction] 1. This Protocol applies to proceedings within England and Wales only . It does not affect the time limit specified by Rule 54.5(1) of the Civil Procedure Rules (CPR), which requires that any claim form in an application for judicial review must be filed promptly and in any event not later than 3 months after the grounds to make the claim first arose. Nor does it affect the shorter time limits specified by Rules 54.5(5) and (6), which set out that a claim form for certain planning judicial reviews must be filed within 6 weeks and the claim form for certain procurement judicial reviews must be filed within 30 days. 1

[Pre-Action Protocol for Judicial Review > Introduction] 2. This Protocol sets out a code of good practice and contains the steps which parties should generally follow before making a claim for judicial review.

## 3. The aims of the protocol are to enable parties to prospective claims to—

[Pre-Action Protocol for Judicial Review > 3. The aims of the protocol are to enable parties to prospective claims to—] (a) understand and properly identify the issues in dispute in the proposed claim and share information and relevant documents;

[Pre-Action Protocol for Judicial Review > 3. The aims of the protocol are to enable parties to prospective claims to—] (b) make informed decisions as to whether and how to proceed;

[Pre-Action Protocol for Judicial Review > 3. The aims of the protocol are to enable parties to prospective claims to—] (c) try to settle the dispute without proceedings or reduce the issues in dispute;

[Pre-Action Protocol for Judicial Review > 3. The aims of the protocol are to enable parties to prospective claims to—] (d) avoid unnecessary expense and keep down the costs of resolving the dispute; and

[Pre-Action Protocol for Judicial Review > 3. The aims of the protocol are to enable parties to prospective claims to—] (e) support the efficient management of proceedings where litigation cannot be avoided.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Judicial Review > 3. The aims of the protocol are to enable parties to prospective claims to—] 4. Judicial review allows people with a sufficient interest in a decision or action by a public body to ask a judge to review the lawfulness of—

[Pre-Action Protocol for Judicial Review > 3. The aims of the protocol are to enable parties to prospective claims to—] an enactment; or

[Pre-Action Protocol for Judicial Review > 3. The aims of the protocol are to enable parties to prospective claims to—] a decision, action or failure to act in relation to the exercise of a public function. 2

[Pre-Action Protocol for Judicial Review > 3. The aims of the protocol are to enable parties to prospective claims to—] 5. Judicial review should only be used where no adequate alternative remedy, such as a right of appeal, is available. Even then, judicial review may not be appropriate in every instance. Claimants are strongly advised to seek appropriate legal advice as soon as possible when considering proceedings. Although the Legal Aid Agency will not normally grant full representation before a letter before claim has been sent and the proposed defendant given a reasonable time to respond, initial funding may be available, for eligible claimants, to cover the work necessary to write this. (See Annex C for more information.)

[Pre-Action Protocol for Judicial Review > 3. The aims of the protocol are to enable parties to prospective claims to—] 6. This protocol will not be appropriate in very urgent cases. In this sort of case, a claim should be made immediately. Examples are where directions have been set for the claimant’s removal from the UK or where there is an urgent need for an interim order to compel a public body to act where it has unlawfully refused to do so, such as where a local housing authority fails to secure interim accommodation for a homeless claimant. A letter before claim, and a claim itself, will not stop the implementation of a disputed decision, though a proposed defendant may agree to take no action until its response letter has been provided. In other cases, the claimant may need to apply to the court for an urgent interim order. Even in very urgent cases, it is good practice to alert the defendant by telephone and to send by email (or fax) to the defendant the draft Claim Form which the claimant intends to issue. A claimant is also normally required to notify a defendant when an interim order is being sought.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Judicial Review > 3. The aims of the protocol are to enable parties to prospective claims to—] 7. All claimants will need to satisfy themselves whether they should follow the protocol, depending upon the circumstances of the case. Where the use of the protocol is appropriate, the court will normally expect all parties to have complied with it in good time before proceedings are issued and will take into account compliance or non-compliance when giving directions for case management of proceedings or when making orders for costs. 3

[Pre-Action Protocol for Judicial Review > 3. The aims of the protocol are to enable parties to prospective claims to—] 8. The Upper Tribunal Immigration and Asylum Chamber (UTIAC) has jurisdiction in respect of judicial review proceedings in relation to most immigration decisions. 4 The President of UTIAC has issued a Practice Statement to the effect that, in judicial review proceedings in UTIAC, the parties will be expected to follow this protocol, where appropriate, as they would for proceedings in the High Court.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Judicial Review > 3. The aims of the protocol are to enable parties to prospective claims to—] Alternative Dispute Resolution

[Pre-Action Protocol for Judicial Review > 3. The aims of the protocol are to enable parties to prospective claims to—] 9. The courts take the view that litigation should be a last resort. The parties should consider whether some form of alternative dispute resolution (‘ADR’) or complaints procedure would be more suitable than litigation, and if so, endeavour to agree which to adopt. Both the claimant and defendant may be required by the court to provide evidence that alternative means of resolving their dispute were considered. Parties are warned that if the protocol is not followed (including this paragraph) then the court must have regard to such conduct when determining costs. However, parties should also note that a claim for judicial review should comply with the time limits set out in the Introduction above. Exploring ADR may not excuse failure to comply with the time limits. If it is appropriate to issue a claim to ensure compliance with a time limit, but the parties agree there should be a stay of proceedings to explore settlement or narrowing the issues in dispute, a joint application for appropriate directions can be made to the court.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Judicial Review > 3. The aims of the protocol are to enable parties to prospective claims to—] 10. It is not practicable in this protocol to address in detail how the parties might decide which method to adopt to resolve their particular dispute. However, summarised below are some of the options for resolving disputes without litigation which may be appropriate, depending on the circumstances—

[Pre-Action Protocol for Judicial Review > 3. The aims of the protocol are to enable parties to prospective claims to—] Discussion and negotiation.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Judicial Review > 3. The aims of the protocol are to enable parties to prospective claims to—] Using relevant public authority complaints or review procedures.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Judicial Review > 3. The aims of the protocol are to enable parties to prospective claims to—] Ombudsmen – the Parliamentary and Health Service and the Local Government Ombudsmen have discretion to deal with complaints relating to maladministration. The British and Irish Ombudsman Association provide information about Ombudsman schemes and other complaint handling bodies and this is available from their website at www.bioa.org.uk (opens in a new tab) . Parties may wish to note that the Ombudsmen are not able to look into a complaint once court action has been commenced.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Judicial Review > 3. The aims of the protocol are to enable parties to prospective claims to—] Mediation – a form of facilitated negotiation assisted by an independent neutral party.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Judicial Review > 3. The aims of the protocol are to enable parties to prospective claims to—] 11. The Civil Justice Council and Judicial College have endorsed The Jackson ADR Handbook by Susan Blake, Julie Browne and Stuart Sime (2013, Oxford University Press). The Citizens Advice Bureaux website also provides information about ADR.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Judicial Review > 3. The aims of the protocol are to enable parties to prospective claims to—] Information is also available at: https://www.gov.uk/guidance/a-guide-to-civil-mediation (opens in a new tab)

[Pre-Action Protocol for Judicial Review > 3. The aims of the protocol are to enable parties to prospective claims to—] 12. If proceedings are issued, the parties may be required by the court to provide evidence that ADR has been considered. A party’s silence in response to an invitation to participate in ADR or refusal to participate in ADR might be considered unreasonable by the court and could lead to the court ordering that party to pay additional court costs.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Judicial Review > 3. The aims of the protocol are to enable parties to prospective claims to—] Requests for information and documents at the pre-action stage

[Pre-Action Protocol for Judicial Review > 3. The aims of the protocol are to enable parties to prospective claims to—] 13. Requests for information and documents made at the pre-action stage should be proportionate and should be limited to what is properly necessary for the claimant to understand why the challenged decision has been taken and/or to present the claim in a manner that will properly identify the issues. The defendant should comply with any request which meets these requirements unless there is good reason for it not to do so. Where the court considers that a public body should have provided relevant documents and/or information, particularly where this failure is a breach of a statutory or common law requirement, it may impose costs sanctions.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Judicial Review > 3. The aims of the protocol are to enable parties to prospective claims to—] The letter before claim

[Pre-Action Protocol for Judicial Review > 3. The aims of the protocol are to enable parties to prospective claims to—] 14. In good time before making a claim, the claimant should send a letter to the defendant. The purpose of this letter is to identify the issues in dispute and establish whether they can be narrowed or litigation can be avoided.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Judicial Review > 3. The aims of the protocol are to enable parties to prospective claims to—] 15. Claimants should normally use the suggested standard format for the letter outlined at Annex A. For Immigration, Nationality and Asylum cases, the Home Office has a standardised form which can be used. It can be found online at: https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/chapter-27-judicial-review-guidance-part-1 (opens in a new tab)

[Pre-Action Protocol for Judicial Review > 3. The aims of the protocol are to enable parties to prospective claims to—] 16. The letter should contain the date and details of the decision, act or omission being challenged, a clear summary of the facts and the legal basis for the claim. It should also contain the details of any information that the claimant is seeking and an explanation of why this is considered relevant. If the claim is considered to be an Aarhus Convention claim (see Rules 45.41 to 45.44 and Practice Direction 45), the letter should state this clearly and explain the reasons, since specific rules as to costs apply to such claims. If the claim is considered appropriate for allocation to the Planning Court and/or for classification as “significant” within that court, the letter should state this clearly and explain the reasons.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Judicial Review > 3. The aims of the protocol are to enable parties to prospective claims to—] 17. The letter should normally contain the details of any person known to the claimant who is an Interested Party. An Interested Party is any person directly affected by the claim. 5 They should be sent a copy of the letter before claim for information. Claimants are strongly advised to seek appropriate legal advice when considering proceedings which involve an Interested Party and, in particular, before sending the letter before claim to an Interested Party or making a claim.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Judicial Review > 3. The aims of the protocol are to enable parties to prospective claims to—] 18. A claim should not normally be made until the proposed reply date given in the letter before the claim has passed, unless the circumstances of the case require more immediate action to be taken. The claimant should send the letter before claim in good time so as to enable a response which can then be taken into account before the time limit for issuing the claim expires, unless there are good reasons why this is not possible.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Judicial Review > 3. The aims of the protocol are to enable parties to prospective claims to—] 19. Any claimant intending to ask for a protective costs order (an order that the claimant will not be liable for the costs of the defendant or any other party or to limit such liability) should explain the reasons for making the request, including an explanation of the limit of the financial resources available to the claimant in making the claim.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Judicial Review > 3. The aims of the protocol are to enable parties to prospective claims to—] The letter of response

[Pre-Action Protocol for Judicial Review > 3. The aims of the protocol are to enable parties to prospective claims to—] 20. Defendants should normally respond within 14 days using the standard format at Annex B. Failure to do so will be taken into account by the court and sanctions may be imposed unless there are good reasons. 6 Where the claimant is a litigant in person, the defendant should enclose a copy of this Protocol with its letter.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Judicial Review > 3. The aims of the protocol are to enable parties to prospective claims to—] 21. Where it is not possible to reply within the proposed time limit, the defendant should send an interim reply and propose a reasonable extension, giving a date by which the defendant expects to respond substantively. Where an extension is sought, reasons should be given and, where required, additional information requested. This will not affect the time limit for making a claim for judicial review 7 nor will it bind the claimant where he or she considers this to be unreasonable. However, where the court considers that a subsequent claim is made prematurely it may impose sanctions.

## 22. If the claim is being conceded in full, the reply should say so in clear and unambiguous terms.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Judicial Review > 22. If the claim is being conceded in full, the reply should say so in clear and unambiguous terms.] 23. If the claim is being conceded in part or not being conceded at all, the reply should say so in clear and unambiguous terms, and—

[Pre-Action Protocol for Judicial Review > 22. If the claim is being conceded in full, the reply should say so in clear and unambiguous terms.] (a) where appropriate, contain a new decision, clearly identifying what aspects of the claim are being conceded and what are not, or, give a clear timescale within which the new decision will be issued;

[Pre-Action Protocol for Judicial Review > 22. If the claim is being conceded in full, the reply should say so in clear and unambiguous terms.] (b) provide a fuller explanation for the decision, if considered appropriate to do so;

[Pre-Action Protocol for Judicial Review > 22. If the claim is being conceded in full, the reply should say so in clear and unambiguous terms.] (c) address any points of dispute, or explain why they cannot be addressed;

[Pre-Action Protocol for Judicial Review > 22. If the claim is being conceded in full, the reply should say so in clear and unambiguous terms.] (d) enclose any relevant documentation requested by the claimant, or explain why the documents are not being enclosed;

[Pre-Action Protocol for Judicial Review > 22. If the claim is being conceded in full, the reply should say so in clear and unambiguous terms.] (e) where documents cannot be provided within the time scales required, then give a clear timescale for provision. The claimant should avoid making any formal application for the provision of documentation/information during this period unless there are good grounds to show that the timescale proposed is unreasonable;

[Pre-Action Protocol for Judicial Review > 22. If the claim is being conceded in full, the reply should say so in clear and unambiguous terms.] (f) where appropriate, confirm whether or not they will oppose any application for an interim remedy; and

[Pre-Action Protocol for Judicial Review > 22. If the claim is being conceded in full, the reply should say so in clear and unambiguous terms.] (g) if the claimant has stated an intention to ask for a protective costs order, the defendant’s response to this should be explained.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Judicial Review > 22. If the claim is being conceded in full, the reply should say so in clear and unambiguous terms.] If the letter before claim has stated that the claim is an Aarhus Convention claim but the defendant does not accept this, the reply should state this clearly and explain the reasons. If the letter before claim has stated that the claim is suitable for the Planning Court and/or categorisation as “significant” within that court but the defendant does not accept this, the reply should state this clearly and explain the reasons.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Judicial Review > 22. If the claim is being conceded in full, the reply should say so in clear and unambiguous terms.] 24. The response should be sent to all Interested Parties 8 identified by the claimant and contain details of any other persons who the defendant considers are Interested Parties.

## ANNEX A

[Pre-Action Protocol for Judicial Review > ANNEX A] Letter before claim

[Pre-Action Protocol for Judicial Review > ANNEX A] Section 1. Information required in a letter before claim

[Pre-Action Protocol for Judicial Review > ANNEX A] 1 Proposed claim for judicial review To (Insert the name and address of the proposed defendant – see details in section 2.)

## 2 The claimant (Insert the title, first and last name and the address of the claimant.)

[Pre-Action Protocol for Judicial Review > 2 The claimant (Insert the title, first and last name and the address of the claimant.)] 3 The defendant’s reference details (When dealing with large organisations it is important to understand that the information relating to any particular individual’s previous dealings with it may not be immediately available, therefore it is important to set out the relevant reference numbers for the matter in dispute and/or the identity of those within the public body who have been handling the particular matter in dispute – see details in section 3.)

[Pre-Action Protocol for Judicial Review > 2 The claimant (Insert the title, first and last name and the address of the claimant.)] 4 The details of the claimants’ legal advisers, if any, dealing with this claim (Set out the name, address and reference details of any legal advisers dealing with the claim.)

[Pre-Action Protocol for Judicial Review > 2 The claimant (Insert the title, first and last name and the address of the claimant.)] 5 The details of the matter being challenged (Set out clearly the matter being challenged, particularly if there has been more than one decision.)

[Pre-Action Protocol for Judicial Review > 2 The claimant (Insert the title, first and last name and the address of the claimant.)] 6 The details of any Interested Parties (Set out the details of any Interested Parties and confirm that they have been sent a copy of this letter.)

[Pre-Action Protocol for Judicial Review > 2 The claimant (Insert the title, first and last name and the address of the claimant.)] 7 The issue (Set out a brief summary of the facts and relevant legal principles, the date and details of the decision, or act or omission being challenged, and why it is contended to be wrong.)

[Pre-Action Protocol for Judicial Review > 2 The claimant (Insert the title, first and last name and the address of the claimant.)] 8 The details of the action that the defendant is expected to take (Set out the details of the remedy sought, including whether a review or any interim remedy are being requested.)

[Pre-Action Protocol for Judicial Review > 2 The claimant (Insert the title, first and last name and the address of the claimant.)] 9 ADR proposals (Set out any proposals the claimant is making to resolve or narrow the dispute by ADR.)

[Pre-Action Protocol for Judicial Review > 2 The claimant (Insert the title, first and last name and the address of the claimant.)] 10 The details of any information sought (Set out the details of any information that is sought which is related to identifiable issues in dispute so as to enable the parties to resolve or reduce those issues. This may include a request for a fuller explanation of the reasons for the decision that is being challenged.)

[Pre-Action Protocol for Judicial Review > 2 The claimant (Insert the title, first and last name and the address of the claimant.)] 11 The details of any documents that are considered relevant and necessary (Set out the details of any documentation or policy in respect of which the disclosure is sought and explain why these are relevant.)

## 12 The address for reply and service of court documents (Insert the address for the reply.)

[Pre-Action Protocol for Judicial Review > 12 The address for reply and service of court documents (Insert the address for the reply.)] 13 Proposed reply date (The precise time will depend upon the circumstances of the individual case. However, although a shorter or longer time may be appropriate in a particular case, 14 days is a reasonable time to allow in most circumstances.)

[Pre-Action Protocol for Judicial Review > 12 The address for reply and service of court documents (Insert the address for the reply.)] Section 2. Address for sending the letter before claim

[Pre-Action Protocol for Judicial Review > 12 The address for reply and service of court documents (Insert the address for the reply.)] Public bodies have requested that, for certain types of cases, in order to ensure a prompt response, letters before claim should be sent to specific addresses.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Judicial Review > 12 The address for reply and service of court documents (Insert the address for the reply.)] Where the claim concerns a decision in an Immigration, Asylum or Nationality case (including in relation to an immigration decision taken abroad by an Entry Clearance Officer)— The claim should be sent electronically to the following Home Office email address: UKVIPAP@homeoffice.gov.uk

[Pre-Action Protocol for Judicial Review > 12 The address for reply and service of court documents (Insert the address for the reply.)] Alternatively the claim may be sent by post to the following Home Office postal address:

[Pre-Action Protocol for Judicial Review > 12 The address for reply and service of court documents (Insert the address for the reply.)] Litigation Allocation Unit 6, New Square Bedfont Lakes Feltham, Middlesex TW14 8HA

[Pre-Action Protocol for Judicial Review > 12 The address for reply and service of court documents (Insert the address for the reply.)] The Home Office has a standardised form which claimants may find helpful to use for communications with the Home Office in Immigration, Asylum or Nationality cases pursuant to this Protocol, to assist claimants to include all relevant information and to promote speedier review and response by the Home Office. The Home Office form may be filled out in electronic or hard copy format. It can be found online at: https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/chapter-27-judicial-review-guidance-part-1 (opens in a new tab)

[Pre-Action Protocol for Judicial Review > 12 The address for reply and service of court documents (Insert the address for the reply.)] Where the claim concerns a decision by the Legal Aid Agency— The address on the decision letter/notification; Legal Director Corporate Legal Team Legal Aid Agency 102 Petty France London SW1H 9AJ

[Pre-Action Protocol for Judicial Review > 12 The address for reply and service of court documents (Insert the address for the reply.)] Where the claim concerns a decision by a local authority— The address on the decision letter/notification; and their legal department 9

[Pre-Action Protocol for Judicial Review > 12 The address for reply and service of court documents (Insert the address for the reply.)] Where the claim concerns a decision by a department or body for whom the Treasury Solicitor acts and the Treasury Solicitor has already been involved in the case, a copy should also be sent, quoting the Treasury Solicitor’s reference, to— The Treasury Solicitor, 102 Petty France, Westminster, London SW1H 9GL

[Pre-Action Protocol for Judicial Review > 12 The address for reply and service of court documents (Insert the address for the reply.)] Where the claim concerns a decision by Her Majesty’s Revenue and Customs— the address on the letter notifying the decision; and General Counsel and Solicitor to Her Majesty’s Revenue and Customs, HM Revenue and Customs, 14 Westfield Avenue, Stratford, London E20 1HZ

[Pre-Action Protocol for Judicial Review > 12 The address for reply and service of court documents (Insert the address for the reply.)] In all other circumstances, the letter should be sent to the address on the letter notifying the decision.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Judicial Review > 12 The address for reply and service of court documents (Insert the address for the reply.)] Section 3. Specific reference details required

[Pre-Action Protocol for Judicial Review > 12 The address for reply and service of court documents (Insert the address for the reply.)] Public bodies have requested that the following information should be provided, if at all possible, in order to ensure prompt response. Where the claim concerns an Immigration, Asylum or Nationality case, dependent upon the nature of the case—

[Pre-Action Protocol for Judicial Review > 12 The address for reply and service of court documents (Insert the address for the reply.)] The Home Office reference number;

[Pre-Action Protocol for Judicial Review > 12 The address for reply and service of court documents (Insert the address for the reply.)] The Port reference number;

[Pre-Action Protocol for Judicial Review > 12 The address for reply and service of court documents (Insert the address for the reply.)] The Asylum and Immigration Tribunal reference number;

[Pre-Action Protocol for Judicial Review > 12 The address for reply and service of court documents (Insert the address for the reply.)] The National Asylum Support Service reference number; or, if these are unavailable:

[Pre-Action Protocol for Judicial Review > 12 The address for reply and service of court documents (Insert the address for the reply.)] The full name, nationality and date of birth of the claimant.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Judicial Review > 12 The address for reply and service of court documents (Insert the address for the reply.)] Where the claim concerns a decision by the Legal Aid Agency—

[Pre-Action Protocol for Judicial Review > 12 The address for reply and service of court documents (Insert the address for the reply.)] The certificate reference number.

## ANNEX B

[Pre-Action Protocol for Judicial Review > ANNEX B] Response to a letter before claim

[Pre-Action Protocol for Judicial Review > ANNEX B] Information required in a response to a letter before claim

[Pre-Action Protocol for Judicial Review > ANNEX B] 1 The claimant (Insert the title, first and last names and the address to which any reply should be sent.)

## 2 From (Insert the name and address of the defendant.)

[Pre-Action Protocol for Judicial Review > 2 From (Insert the name and address of the defendant.)] 3 Reference details (Set out the relevant reference numbers for the matter in dispute and the identity of those within the public body who have been handling the issue.)

[Pre-Action Protocol for Judicial Review > 2 From (Insert the name and address of the defendant.)] 4 The details of the matter being challenged (Set out details of the matter being challenged, providing a fuller explanation of the decision, where this is considered appropriate.)

[Pre-Action Protocol for Judicial Review > 2 From (Insert the name and address of the defendant.)] 5 Response to the proposed claim (Set out whether the issue in question is conceded in part, or in full, or will be contested. Where an interim reply is being sent and there is a realistic prospect of settlement, details should be included. If the claimant is a litigant in person, a copy of the Pre-Action Protocol should be enclosed with the letter.)

[Pre-Action Protocol for Judicial Review > 2 From (Insert the name and address of the defendant.)] 6 Details of any other Interested Parties (Identify any other parties who you consider have an interest who have not already been sent a letter by the claimant.)

[Pre-Action Protocol for Judicial Review > 2 From (Insert the name and address of the defendant.)] 7 ADR proposals (Set out the defendant’s position on any ADR proposals made in the letter before claim and any ADR proposals by the defendant.)

[Pre-Action Protocol for Judicial Review > 2 From (Insert the name and address of the defendant.)] 8 Response to requests for information and documents (Set out the defendant’s answer to the requests made in the letter before claim including reasons why any requested information or documents are not being disclosed.)

[Pre-Action Protocol for Judicial Review > 2 From (Insert the name and address of the defendant.)] 9 Address for further correspondence and service of court documents (Set out the address for any future correspondence on this matter)

## ANNEX C

[Pre-Action Protocol for Judicial Review > ANNEX C] Notes on public funding for legal costs in judicial review

[Pre-Action Protocol for Judicial Review > ANNEX C] Public funding for legal costs in judicial review is available from legal professionals and advice agencies which have contracts with the Legal Aid Agency. Funding may be provided for—

[Pre-Action Protocol for Judicial Review > ANNEX C] Legal Help to provide initial advice and assistance with any legal problem; or

[Pre-Action Protocol for Judicial Review > ANNEX C] Legal Representation to allow you to be represented in court if you are taking or defending court proceedings. This is available in two forms—

[Pre-Action Protocol for Judicial Review > ANNEX C] Investigative Help is limited to funding to investigate the strength of the proposed claim. It includes the issue and conduct of proceedings only so far as is necessary to obtain disclosure of relevant information or to protect the client’s position in relation to any urgent hearing or time limit for the issue of proceedings. This includes the work necessary to write a letter before claim to the body potentially under challenge, setting out the grounds of challenge, and giving that body a reasonable opportunity, typically 14 days, in which to respond.  Full Representation is provided to represent you in legal proceedings and includes litigation services, advocacy services, and all such help as is usually given by a person providing representation in proceedings, including steps preliminary or incidental to proceedings, and/or arriving at or giving effect to a compromise to avoid or bring to an end any proceedings. Except in emergency cases, a proper letter before claim must be sent and the other side must be given an opportunity to respond before Full Representation is granted.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Judicial Review > ANNEX C] Further information on the type(s) of help available and the criteria for receiving that help may be found in the Legal Aid Agency’s pages on the Ministry of Justice website at: https://www.justice.gov.uk/legal-aid (opens in a new tab)

[Pre-Action Protocol for Judicial Review > ANNEX C] A list of contracted firms and Advice Agencies may be found at: http://find-legal-advice.justice.gov.uk (opens in a new tab) ”

## Footnotes

[Pre-Action Protocol for Judicial Review > Footnotes] 1. The court has a discretion to extend time. It cannot be taken that compliance with the protocol will of itself be sufficient to excuse delay or justify an extension of time, but it may be a relevant factor. Under rule 54.5(2), judicial review time limits cannot be extended by agreement between the parties. Also, the High Court can order the transfer of judicial review proceedings to the UTIAC. Return to footnote 4

Document: Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents
Section: 5.9
Part 2 of 4
==================================================
## 5.9

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 5.9] (1) Where the claimant reasonably believes that the claim is valued at above the limit in paragraph (2) but at no more than the Protocol upper limit, but it subsequently becomes apparent that the value of the claim is below the limit in paragraph (2), the claimant is entitled to the Stage 1 and (where relevant) the Stage 2 fixed costs.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 5.9] (2) The limit referred to in paragraph (1) above is £5,000 for damages for personal injury and £10,000 in total and is limited to claims where the claimant is not a child.

## 5.9A

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 5.9A] (1) Subject to paragraph (2), where a claim has started in the RTA Small Claims Protocol and the defendant has notified the claimant that they consider the overall claim is likely to be valued at more than £10,000 or the claim for damages for injury is likely to be valued at more than £5,000, this Protocol should be applied starting at paragraph 6.1.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 5.9A] (2) Paragraph (1) applies only where—

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 5.9A] (a) the defendant also notifies the claimant that they consider that the claim is worth no more than the Protocol upper limit;

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 5.9A] (b) the claim is not one which was started in the RTA Protocol and no longer continued in that protocol; and

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 5.9A] (c) either—

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 5.9A] (i) there was an admission of liability in full under this Protocol within the response period;

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 5.9A] (ii) there was an admission of liability in full but subject to an argument that the claimant contributed to their injuries by not wearing a seatbelt (where the claimant admitted not doing so); or

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 5.9A] (iii) the period for a liability response under this Protocol has not yet expired.

## Claimants without a legal representative

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > Claimants without a legal representative] 5.10 Where the claimant does not have a legal representative, on receipt of the CNF the defendant must—

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > Claimants without a legal representative] (1) explain the period within which a response is required;

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > Claimants without a legal representative] (2) explain that the claimant may obtain independent legal advice; and

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > Claimants without a legal representative] (3) undertake a search of askCUEPI (website at: www.askCUE.co.uk (opens in a new tab) ) or an equivalent search system for defendants.

## 5.10A Where the claimant does not have a legal representative, paragraph 6.3A does not apply.

## Discontinuing the Protocol process

## 5.11 Claims which no longer continue under this Protocol cannot subsequently re-enter the process.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 5.11 Claims which no longer continue under this Protocol cannot subsequently re-enter the process.] To the top

## SECTION III – THE STAGES OF THE PROCESS

## Stage 1

## Completion of the Claim Notification Form

## 6.1 The claimant must complete and send—

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 6.1 The claimant must complete and send—] (1) the CNF to the defendant’s insurer; and

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 6.1 The claimant must complete and send—] (2) the ‘Defendant Only CNF’ to the defendant by first class post, except where the defendant is a self-insurer in which case the CNF must be sent to the defendant as insurer and no ‘Defendant Only CNF’ is required.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 6.1 The claimant must complete and send—] 6.2 The ‘Defendant Only CNF’ must be sent at the same time or as soon as practicable after the CNF is sent.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 6.1 The claimant must complete and send—] 6.3 All boxes in the CNF that are marked as mandatory must be completed before it is sent.  The claimant must make a reasonable attempt to complete those boxes that are not marked as mandatory.

## 6.3A

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 6.3A] (1) Before the CNF is sent to the defendant pursuant to paragraph 6.1, the claimant’s legal representative must undertake a search of askCUEPI (website at: www.askCUE.co.uk (opens in a new tab) ) and must enter in the additional information box in the CNF the unique reference number generated by that search.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 6.3A] (2) Where the claimant has sent the CNF without the unique reference number required by subparagraph (1), the defendant may require the claimant to resend the CNF with the reference number inserted. The period in paragraph 6.11 or 6.13 starts from the date the CNF was sent with the unique reference number.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 6.3A] (3) Where the claimant has sent the CNF without the unique reference number required by subparagraph (1) and the defendant does not require the claimant to resend the CNF pursuant to subparagraph (2), the defendant must respond in accordance with paragraph 6.11 or 6.13.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 6.3A] 6.4 A claim for vehicle related damages will ordinarily be dealt with outside the provisions of this Protocol under industry agreements between relevant organisations and insurers.  Where there is a claim for vehicle related damages the claimant must—

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 6.3A] (1) state in the CNF that the claim is being dealt with by a third party; or

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 6.3A] (2)

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 6.3A] (a) explain in the CNF that the legal representative is dealing with the recovery of these additional amounts; and

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 6.3A] (b) attach any relevant invoices and receipts to the CNF or explain when they are likely to be sent to the defendant.

## 6.5 Where the claimant is a child, this must be noted in the relevant section of the CNF.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 6.5 Where the claimant is a child, this must be noted in the relevant section of the CNF.] 6.6 The statement of truth in the CNF must be signed either by the claimant or by the claimant’s legal representative where the claimant has authorised the legal representative to do so and the legal representative can produce written evidence of that authorisation. Where the claimant is a child the statement of truth may be signed by the parent or guardian. On the electronically completed CNF the person may enter their name in the signature box to satisfy this requirement.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 6.5 Where the claimant is a child, this must be noted in the relevant section of the CNF.] To the top

## Rehabilitation

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > Rehabilitation] 6.7 The claimant must set out details of rehabilitation in the CNF. The parties should at all stages consider the Rehabilitation Code which may be found at: http://www.iua.co.uk/IUA_Member/Publications (opens in a new tab)

## Failure to complete the Claim Notification Form

## 6.8

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 6.8] (1) Subject to subparagraph (2) and paragraph 6.3A(2), where the defendant considers that inadequate mandatory information has been provided in the CNF, that shall be a valid reason for the defendant to decide that the claim should no longer continue under this Protocol.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 6.8] (2) Where the claimant has sent the CNF to the defendant without the unique reference number required by paragraph 6.3A(1), but the defendant does not require the claimant to resend the CNF with the reference number inserted pursuant to paragraph 6.3A(2), the fact that the claimant has not provided this information shall not be a valid reason for the defendant to decide that the claim should no longer continue under this Protocol.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 6.8] 6.9 Rule 45.35(2) and (3) sets out the sanctions available to the court where it considers that the claimant provided inadequate information in the CNF.

## Response from insurer

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > Response from insurer] 6.10 The defendant must send to the claimant an electronic acknowledgment the next day after receipt of the CNF.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > Response from insurer] 6.11 The defendant must complete the ‘Insurer Response’ section of the CNF (“the CNF response”) and send it to the claimant within 15 days.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > Response from insurer] To the top

## Application for a certificate of recoverable benefits

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > Application for a certificate of recoverable benefits] 6.12 The defendant must, before the end of Stage 1, apply to the Compensation Recovery Unit (CRU) for a certificate of recoverable benefits.

## Motor Insurers’ Bureau

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > Motor Insurers’ Bureau] 6.13 Where no insurer is identified and the claim falls to be dealt with by the MIB or its agents the CNF response must be completed and sent to the claimant within 30 days.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > Motor Insurers’ Bureau] 6.14 Where the MIB passes the claim to an insurer to act on its behalf, that insurer must notify the claimant of that fact. There is no extension to the time period in paragraph 6.13.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > Motor Insurers’ Bureau] To the top

## Contributory negligence, liability not admitted or failure to respond

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > Contributory negligence, liability not admitted or failure to respond] 6.15 The claim will no longer continue under this Protocol where the defendant, within the period in paragraph 6.11 or 6.13—

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > Contributory negligence, liability not admitted or failure to respond] (1) makes an admission of liability but alleges contributory negligence (other than in relation to the claimant’s admitted failure to wear a seat belt);

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > Contributory negligence, liability not admitted or failure to respond] (2) does not complete and send the CNF response;

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > Contributory negligence, liability not admitted or failure to respond] (3) does not admit liability; or

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > Contributory negligence, liability not admitted or failure to respond] (4) notifies the claimant that the defendant considers that—

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > Contributory negligence, liability not admitted or failure to respond] (a) there is inadequate mandatory information in the CNF; or

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > Contributory negligence, liability not admitted or failure to respond] (b)  if proceedings were issued, the small claims track would be the normal track for that claim.

## 6.15A Where—

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 6.15A Where—] (a) paragraph 6.15(4)(b) applies;

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 6.15A Where—] (b) the date of the accident is on or after 31 st May 2021; and

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 6.15A Where—] (c) the parties have agreed that the RTA Small Claims Protocol applies,

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 6.15A Where—] the claimant must start a claim by following that Protocol, starting at paragraph 5.3.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 6.15A Where—] 6.16 Where the defendant does not admit liability under paragraph 6.15(3), the defendant must give brief reasons in the CNF response.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 6.15A Where—] 6.17 Where paragraph 6.15 applies the claim will proceed under the Pre-Action Protocol for Personal Injury Claims starting at paragraph 6.3 of that Protocol (which allows a maximum of three months for the defendant to investigate the claim) except that where paragraph 6.15(4)(a) applies the claim will proceed under paragraph 5.1 of that Protocol.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 6.15A Where—] (For admissions made in the course of the process under this Protocol, see rule 14.1B.)

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 6.15A Where—] (Paragraph 2.10A of the Pre-Action Protocol on Personal Injury provides that the CNF can be used as the letter of claim except where the claim no longer continues under this Protocol because the CNF contained inadequate information.)

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 6.15A Where—] To the top

## Stage 1 fixed costs

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > Stage 1 fixed costs] 6.18 Except where the claimant is a child, the defendant must pay the Stage 1 fixed costs in Table 10 of Practice Direction 45 and, in a soft tissue injury claim, the cost of obtaining the fixed cost medical report and any cost for obtaining medical records in rule 45.62(2) (collectively the “Stage 1 fixed recoverable costs”) where—

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > Stage 1 fixed costs] (1) liability is admitted; or

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > Stage 1 fixed costs] (2) liability is admitted and contributory negligence is alleged only in relation to the claimant’s admitted failure to wear a seat belt, within 10 days after receiving the Stage 2 Settlement Pack, provided that invoices for the cost of obtaining the medical report and any medical records in a soft tissue injury claim have been included in the Stage 2 Settlement Pack.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > Stage 1 fixed costs] 6.19 Where the defendant fails to pay the Stage 1 fixed recoverable costs within the period specified in paragraph 6.18 the claimant may give written notice that the claim will no longer continue under this Protocol. Unless the claimant’s notice is sent to the defendant within 10 days after the expiry of the period in paragraph 6.18 the claim will continue under this Protocol.

## Defendant’s account of the accident in soft tissue injury claims

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > Defendant’s account of the accident in soft tissue injury claims] 6.19A Where liability is admitted in a soft tissue injury claim, it is expected that in most cases the defendant’s account will not be relevant to the procedure in Stage 2. In the limited cases where it is considered appropriate, the defendant may send their account to the claimant electronically at the same time as the CNF response. The defendant’s insurer must have the defendant’s written authority to provide this account and, in sending it, is certifying that it has that authority. For the purposes of this paragraph, the defendant’s written authority may be provided electronically.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > Defendant’s account of the accident in soft tissue injury claims] 6.19B The procedure in paragraph 6.19A applies to the MIB, save that the MIB is certifying that the defendant user of the vehicle has provided such authority.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > Defendant’s account of the accident in soft tissue injury claims] To the top

## Stage 2

## Medical Reports – all claims

## 7.1

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 7.1] (1) Save where paragraph (2) applies, the clamant should obtain a medical report, if one has not already been obtained.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 7.1] (2) In claims which consist of or include a whiplash injury, the claimant must obtain a medical report in accordance with paragraph 7.8C.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 7.1] 7.2 It is expected that most claimants will obtain a medical report from one expert, but additional medical reports may be obtained from other experts where the injuries require reports from more than one medical discipline.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 7.1] 7.3 The claimant must check the factual accuracy of any medical report before it is sent to the defendant.  There will be no further opportunity for the claimant to challenge the factual accuracy of a medical report after it has been sent to the defendant.

## 7.4

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 7.4] (1) The medical expert should identify within the report—

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 7.4] (a) the medical records that have been reviewed; and

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 7.4] (b) the medical records considered relevant to the claim.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 7.4] (2) The claimant must disclose with any medical report sent to the defendant any medical records which the expert considers relevant.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 7.4] 7.5 In most claims with a value of no more than £10,000, it is expected that the medical expert will not need to see any medical records.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 7.4] 7.6 Any relevant photograph(s) of the claimant’s injuries upon which the claimant intends to rely should also be disclosed with the medical report.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 7.4] 7.7 Where the claimant was not wearing a seat belt the medical report must contain sufficient information to enable the defendant to calculate the appropriate reduction of damages in accordance with principles set out in existing case law.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 7.4] To the top

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 7.4] 7.8 A subsequent medical report from an expert who has already reported must be justified. A report may be justified where—

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 7.4] (1) the first medical report recommends that further time is required before a prognosis of the claimant’s injuries can be determined; or

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 7.4] (2) the claimant is receiving continuing treatment; or

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 7.4] (3) the claimant has not recovered as expected in the original prognosis.

## Soft tissue injury claims – medical reports

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > Soft tissue injury claims – medical reports] 7.8A In addition to paragraphs 7.1 to 7.7, and subject to paragraph 7.8B, in a soft tissue injury claim—

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > Soft tissue injury claims – medical reports] (1) the first report must be a fixed cost medical report from an accredited medical expert selected for the claim via the MedCo Portal (website at: www.medco.org.uk (opens in a new tab) ); and

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > Soft tissue injury claims – medical reports] (2) where the defendant provides a different account under paragraph 6.19A, the claimant must provide this as part of the instructions to the medical expert for the sole purpose of asking the expert to comment on the impact, if any, on diagnosis and prognosis if—

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > Soft tissue injury claims – medical reports] (a) the claimant’s account is found to be true; or

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > Soft tissue injury claims – medical reports] (b) the defendant’s account is found to be true.

## 7.8B In a soft tissue injury claim—

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 7.8B In a soft tissue injury claim—] (1) it is expected that only one medical report will be required;

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 7.8B In a soft tissue injury claim—] (2) a further medical report, whether from the first expert instructed or from an expert in another discipline, will only be justified where—

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 7.8B In a soft tissue injury claim—] (a) it is recommended in the first expert’s report; and

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 7.8B In a soft tissue injury claim—] (b) that report has first been disclosed to the defendant; and

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 7.8B In a soft tissue injury claim—] (3) where the claimant obtains more than one medical report, the first report must be a fixed cost medical report from an accredited medical expert selected via the MedCo Portal and any further report from an expert in any of the following disciplines must also be a fixed cost medical report—

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 7.8B In a soft tissue injury claim—] (a) Consultant Orthopaedic Surgeon;

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 7.8B In a soft tissue injury claim—] (b) Consultant in Accident and Emergency Medicine;

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 7.8B In a soft tissue injury claim—] (c) General Practitioner registered with the General Medical Council;

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 7.8B In a soft tissue injury claim—] (d) Physiotherapist registered with the Health and Care Professions Council.

## Claims which consist of, or include, a claim for whiplash injury – Medical Reports

## 7.8C

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 7.8C] (1) The provisions of paragraph 7.8A and 7.8B apply in respect of a medical report obtained under this paragraph, save that—

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 7.8C] (a) any reference to soft tissue injury claim is to be read as referring to a claim which consists of, or includes, a claim for whiplash injury;

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 7.8C] (b) paragraph (2) below applies in place of paragraph 7.8B(2).

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 7.8C] (2) A further report, whether from the first expert instructed or from an expert in another discipline, will only be justified where—

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 7.8C] (a) it is recommended in the first expert’s report;

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 7.8C] (b) the first medical report recommends that further time is required before a prognosis of the claimant’s injuries can be determined;

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 7.8C] (c) the claimant is receiving continuing treatment; or

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 7.8C] (d) the claimant has not recovered as expected in the original prognosis.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 7.8C] To the top

## Non-medical expert reports

## 7.9

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 7.9] (1) In most cases, a report from a non-medical expert will not be required, but a report may be obtained where it is reasonably required to value the claim.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 7.9] (2) Paragraph 7.3 applies to non-medical expert reports as it applies to expert medical reports.

## Specialist legal advice

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > Specialist legal advice] 7.10 In most cases under this Protocol, it is expected that the claimant’s legal representative will be able to value the claim. In some cases with a value of more than £10,000 (excluding vehicle related damages), an additional advice from a specialist solicitor or from counsel may be justified where it is reasonably required to value the claim.

## Witness statements

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > Witness statements] 7.11 In most cases, witness statements, whether from the claimant or otherwise, will not be, required.   One or more statements may, however, be provided where reasonably required to value the claim.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > Witness statements] To the top

## Stay of process

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > Stay of process] 7.12 Where the claimant needs to obtain a subsequent expert medical report or a non-medical report, the parties should agree to stay the process in this Protocol for a suitable period.  The claimant may then request an interim payment in accordance with paragraphs 7.13 to 7.16.
